summary: tmk, two gaps remain: a guard startup race and an executable rejection marked bare. Review confined to the target; no files written or evidence blocks executed.

findings.title: [P2] Establish launcher identity before the guard starts
findings.body: Checking whether the parent changes misses a launcher killed before the guard first records its parent. The guard can observe its adopted parent from its first instruction onward, start the command, and never detect a change. That leaves children running despite the launcher-only SIGKILL guarantee at lines 534–536. The descendant-cleanup revision does not cover this startup window.
findings.recommendation: Specify that the guard receives the expected launcher identity and checks it before starting the command and during monitoring. Require a test where the launcher dies before guard initialization.

findings.title: [P2] Demonstrate the modification-time rejection
findings.body: The bare reason says no block can show a missing signal, but the rejection includes an executable claim: modification time can change before writing finishes. A bounded temporary-file probe can pause a writer after its first chunk and demonstrate that a polling reader observes incomplete output. The separate claim about failed compiles also needs evidence or a narrower formulation. This is an empirical rejection, not merely an architectural preference.
findings.recommendation: Add a deterministic partial-write counterexample and cite it from this row. Establish the failed-compile claim separately, or remove it if the partial-write counterexample is sufficient grounds for rejection.
